memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then the eyes of both of them were opened, and they realized they were naked; so they sewed fig leaves together and made coverings for themselves. — Gen 3:7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The serpent had promised that their eyes would be opened — and in a bitter way, they were. But what a cruel disappointment it turned out to be. They had hoped to see like God; instead, for the first time, they saw their own shame.

Just moments before, Adam and Eve had stood naked and unashamed (Gen 2:25). Now the same nakedness fills them with fear and embarrassment. Nothing about their bodies had changed — but everything inside them had. Sin had entered, and with it came guilt, self-consciousness, and the urge to hide. This is what sin always does. It promises to make life fuller and only leaves us more exposed and afraid.

And notice their response: they sew fig leaves together. It is the first religion in history — human beings trying to cover their own shame by their own effort. But fig leaves wither, and no covering we stitch for ourselves can deal with the guilt underneath.

Dear friend, our best efforts to hide or fix our sin are only fig leaves. They never quite cover us. But God does not leave us in our flimsy coverings. In time He would clothe them Himself (Gen 3:21), pointing forward to the day when Christ would cover us completely — not with leaves, but with His own righteousness (Gal 3:27). The shame we cannot hide, He is able to take away.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What "fig leaves" do you reach for to cover your own shame or guilt?
2. How does it comfort you that God Himself provides the covering we cannot make?
3. Is there something you have been hiding that you need to bring honestly to God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I confess that I often try to cover my sin with my own efforts, like flimsy fig leaves that never truly hide it. Thank You that in Christ You have clothed me with His righteousness. Help me to stop hiding and to rest in the covering only You can provide. Amen.
